[TEXT] In Siege Storeroom
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=262
[TEXT] 
You are in a hidden storeroom filled with stores. A barricade has been set up in front of the door here. The Hospital is South.  

[MSG] cmd=SETZCOLOR a1=0 a2=16633879 a3=0 len=0
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=4834
[TEXT] 
You see a movement behind the barricade and then you hear the click of a trigger. You instinctively raise the shield to protect yourself as a crossbow bolt whirrs towards you and hits the shield, ricocheting away.

You hear a curse then a young man stands up from where he was concealed behind the barricade. He raises both hands in the air, one of which is still holding the crossbow he used to shoot you with.

The man starts to talk to you pleadingly in Prussian, but you hold your hands out to show him you are unarmed and make him understand that you mean him no harm. He realises that you cannot speak his language and he indicates that you are to wait here, and he walks over to a cabinet on the back wall of the storeroom. 
 
You see him unlock the cabinet and he takes something from it and returns to you. He is carrying a small vial and he mimes drinking the liquid in it and hands it to you. You do as he asks and you drink the sickly-looking green liquid, which tastes absolutely vile. You experience a momentary dizziness, which passes quickly. The man starts to talk again and to your astonishment you can understand him.
 
The man tells you his name is Walther and he is one of the manual workers. He relates how he was working in this storeroom when Wladyslaw's forces attacked the castle at dawn the previous day before most of the few knights that were in the fortress at the time had risen. "They appeared out of nowhere and took everyone by surprise," he tells you. "They must have known that most of the knights had left the day before to go to the aid of the people of a village who were being attacked by outlaws. I had just enough time to shut myself in here before they burst into the hospital. I thought it would only be a matter of time before they found how to get in here. I found a crossbow to defend myself but only had one bolt - as you know. I thought you were one of them."

You tell Walther what has transpired since he shut himself in here and about the task Wladyslaw has set you. He hands you the crossbow. "If you can find some bolts for this it might serve you well," he advises you. You tell Walther to stay in this room and that you will hopefully come to tell him the coast is clear when you have defeated Wladyslaw. What will happen if you fail is left unsaid. Walther bids you good luck and you leave the room. As you enter the hospital, the door slides shut behind you.

[MSG] cmd=SETZCOLOR a1=0 a2=16633879 a3=0 len=0
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=928
[TEXT] 
You hear a loud cawing noise which startles you slightly, and you look up to see a couple of large black crows looking down at you from a rooftop on the east side of the bailey. You shiver as you wonder if they would peck out your eyeballs if you were a corpse lying on the ground. Picking up a pebble lying on the ground, you throw it at the crows, which squawk in alarm. They launch themselves off the rooftop and flap away over the granaries toward the river.

[TEXT] 
Now he has all three ingredients, the baker sets to work. You watch, mouth agape, as the ghost whizzes around the bakery, mixing the ingredients, kneading the dough, putting the dough into a tin and then putting that into one of the ovens. After only a few minutes, he takes the tin out of the oven using the paddle you gave to him earlier and you smell the wonderful aroma of freshly baked bread.

He tips the baked loaf of bread out of the tin, cuts a thick slice from it and hands it to you. "I thank you, Duke Alaric," the ghost tells you. "I will have the rest of the bread for my lunch." As his ghostly form starts to fade he extends his arm towards you and you see that he is holding the silver key - now whole - in his hand. "I have repaired your key, you will be able to open the other door now," he tells you as you take it from him.

As you mutter an astonished "Thank you," the ghost nods his head and fades from view.

The bakery is dominated by the huge brick-built kilns in which the bread for the fortress was baked. In front of each of the four kilns is a large wooden table on which the dough was kneaded. Also here is a small hessian sack.

You see a movement out of the corner of your eye and see the ghost of the farrier walking towards you. He stops when he reaches you and picks up the pail.

"I beg your pardon, Duke Alaric," he says apologetically. "I need the pail to fetch water for my horses."

He walks away taking the pail with him, fading from view as he goes, but just as his form disappears for ever you hear his voice whisper, "You won't be needing it again anyway."

As you approach the wall on the south side of the courtyard you look to your right and see the man, whom you saw earlier, standing on the middle of the footbridge over the moat. You notice he is dressed in a robe and he just stands there looking at you, his arms akimbo. You guess that he is Prince Wladyslaw himself.

"Let's see how you get past this!" he calls out to you in a heavily-accented voice and, raising his arms to point at the gatehouse, he mouths the words of an incantation. You instinctively flinch as the archway under the gatehouse is filled with a corruscation of purple and red sparks, accompanied by a loud sizzling noise and a lot of white smoke!

When the pyrotechnic display clears, you see that a solid wall now fills the archway. When you look over at the footbridge again, Wladyslaw is no longer in sight.

[MSG] cmd=SETZCOLOR a1=0 a2=16633879 a3=0 len=0
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=1946
[TEXT] 
As you walk into the refectory you are aware of the faint smell of almonds in the air and the rustle of paper. Then you notice the ghostly figure of an old man sitting at one of the tables, eating something from a paper bag he holds in his hand. As you approach the ghost of the Cellarer - for it can be only he - the figure gets to his feet and inclines his head in greeting.

"I see you found my note, Duke Alaric," he says in a quavering voice. "Thank you for coming. I have been instructed to give you a cryptic clue to help with your mission, and it is this: 'Advisorily speaking, it is a colourful and uplifting way to gain entry to those places you cannot yet reach.'"

As you try to work out the meaning of his speech, his spectral form starts to fade away. Before you have a chance to speak, he raises his hand in farewell, saying, "Pray for me, Duke Alaric, good luck!" As he disappears from view you catch the scent of almonds and a rustle of paper once again.

[TEXT] You quietly talk to the alchemist in an effort to wake him up. After the first couple of tries there is no response and you fear he may be dead, but on the third attempt his eyes flutter open. He gasps in fear but you quickly reassure the old man that you mean him no harm. You tell him who you are and why you are here. The alchemist tells you how he fought a duel arcane with Wladyslaw, who proved the stronger.

"The wizard thought he had killed me, but although my wounds are mortal I managed to crawl back here," the alchemist tells you. Feeling that the old man's time is near, you ask him if there is anything you can do for him?

"Yes! There is something you can do for me," the alchemist tells you, hope flaring in his eyes. "You must concoct an elixir which will enable my spirit to enter the netherworld when my body dies. Find me something to write on and I will write down the ingredients."

You search around for something to write on and with, but all you can find is a piece of calfskin and a scrap of charcoal, which you hand to the alchemist. "Most of the ingredients will be found around the fortress," he informs you. "However, the last one may give you a bit of trouble. If my assistant Hans were still alive he would be able to help you, but I fear he perished during the battle. Use the worktable downstairs to make the Elixir on."

You take the calfskin from the alchemist, who sinks back onto his bed with exhaustion. As he falls into a sleep he may not wake up from you hear him whisper, "Do not fail me, Alaric Blackmoon, the success of your mission depends on this!"

[TEXT] 
You hear a noise behind you and turn to see the stooped figure of a ancient old man standing in the doorway, his wizened face has an angered look upon it.

"How dare thee enter my chamber unbidden!" he says angrily. "Get thee gone...." He breaks off as he sees the statuette you have just put into the niche.

"That is my lost statuette, where didst thou find it!?" he asks you, his angry face now one of astonishment. You tell the old man you found it under the alchemist's bed.

"So that is where it was all these years!" He says incredulously. "I remember showing some of the statuettes to my friend the Alchemist, I must have dropped it and it rolled under his bed."

The old man shuffles up to you and looks up into your face. "Who art thou, and how do you come to be in my domain?" You tell him who you are and what has happened in the fortress above ground. "I am the Custodian of the Catacombs. The affairs of the world above are no longer any concern of mine," he tells you, waving his hand in dismissal.

The ancient old man turns to leave the chamber. "You have my gratitude, Duke Alaric," he tells you. "However, I must now return to my duties." He shuffles out of the chamber into the catacombs.

[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=980
[TEXT] 
"The only place I know of where thee will find that is deep underground. It is some distance from here and the journey is not without its perils." The Custodian frowns at you as if struggling to decide whether to help you or not. After a minute or two he sighs and then speaks.

"As you have restored my lost statuette, I will aid thee, Duke Alaric," the Custodian tells you. "Follow me and do not wander from the path I take."

He shuffles off into the gloom and you follow him closely.


[MSG] cmd=SETZCOLOR a1=0 a2=16633879 a3=0 len=0
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=2238
[TEXT] 
The Custodian leads you further into the catacombs and soon you realise you are heading deep underground. The path is initially along a tortuous passageway which is little more than a well-trodden fissure in the rock.

As you progress you feel the air getting warmer and the rock walls either side of you are indeed warm to the touch. The path you are taking twists and turns, and soon you become disoriented, your natural sense of direction becoming confused.

After about half an hour the passage opens into a vast cavern, filled with gigantic translucent crystal growths which sparkle in the light from your lantern. You stop briefly, mouth agape, to stare at the wondrous formations jutting at all angles from every surface of the cavern.

You are startled out of your reverie by an echoing shout from the Custodian. "Cease thy rubber necking, Duke Alaric, this is no time for sightseeing!"

You hurry to catch up to him and enter another tunnel at the far end of the cavern where you continue descending, the air growing warmer with every step.

Eventually you emerge from the tunnel onto a vast plateau of rock.

You stand at the entrance to the subterranean tunnel which leads back to the catacombs. "Yonder is the edge of hell, Duke Alaric," the Custodian tells you in a fearful voice. "I will remain here to await thy return." He points to your lantern, saying, "Why doest thou not leave thy lantern with me? It will act as a beacon for thee to walk to when thou hast completed thy task."

You hand over your lantern and the custodian nods his head in salute to you. "Good luck, my lord, I think thou may need it!"

[TEXT] Edge of Rock Cliff
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=2234
[TEXT] 
You are standing at the edge of an underground cliff, overlooking a river of molten lava. The lava flows swiftly about 150 feet below the cliff edge and the glow from it bathes your surrounding in a deep red light. The heat rising from the lava is tremendous and it sucks the moisture from your body. Turning around, you see in the distance the Custodian standing by the tunnel entrance, holding your lantern.   Hammered into the ground about a metre and a half from the cliff is a metal spike.  Looped over this is one end of your rope, the other end of which hangs down over the edge of the cliff.  Also here is a piece of paper, a piece of glass, a large shield, a sheet of parchment, a small knife, a needle, a small hessian sack, a glass vial, a saw, a rake, a trowel, a mattock, a sheet of vellum, a red crystal, a screwdriver, a large book, a pig's bladder, a short piece of wood, a square of calfskin, a sheet of papyrus, a swallow's egg, a hen's egg, a withered rose, a green crystal, a broken figurine of a mounted knight, a length of twine, a large hammer, a chainmail haubergeon and the fortress plan.

[TEXT] By Entrance to Tunnel
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=1202
[TEXT] 
You stand at the entrance to the subterranean tunnel which leads back to the catacombs. Your lantern reveals that you are in a huge cleft in the rock, and the roof is only a handful of inches above your head here, but it slopes upwards as the cleft widens. You have no idea of direction down here but ahead you can see what appears to be the edge of the cleft as there is a sharp-edged line against the red glow which comes from below. The edge is about 50 yards away and it would take you only a minute or so to walk to it.  Standing here, leaning on his staff, is the Custodian of the Catacombs.  

[MSG] cmd=SETZCOLOR a1=0 a2=16633879 a3=0 len=0
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=1254
[TEXT] 
You take the lump of pumice from your scrip and triumphantly show it to the Custodian.

"Well done, Duke Alaric," he tells you. "I knew thou couldst succeed!"

The old man returns your lantern to you and he points to the tunnel.

"We must now return to the catacombs. Please keep up - and no rubber-necking!"

The custodian sets off along the tunnel, with you following behind. The journey is uneventful and, despite his warning, you cannot help but gaze about you as the two of you traverse the cavern of crystals.

Eventually you reach the catacombs and the Custodian leads you to the passageway that leads to the stairway.

[TEXT] You gently shake the alchemist's shoulder to wake him up again. His eyes open, he sees the glass flagon with the Elixir in it and he manages to smile weakly.

"I am amazed, Duke Alaric, you have succeeded!" the Alchemist whispers in a frail voice. "Quickly, for I feel that my time is nigh, you will have to hold the flagon to my lips, I have no strength left."

You put one hand under the old man's shoulders and raise him up a little, then you hold the flagon to his lips and tip it up. He slowly drinks the Elixir down, coughing once or twice.

When he has drunk all of it, you lay him back down again. His hand suddenly reaches up to grab the front of your jacket and he pulls your face close to his with the last bit of strength left in his grievously wounded body.

"I will help you where I was unable to help myself, Duke Alaric," the old man tells you. He reaches up and takes your amulet in his hand and whispers the incantation of a magic spell. The amulet glows briefly and the Alchemist releases it.

"I have set a ward on your amulet that will protect you from the kind of magic Wladyslaw will use to kill you. Had I known beforehand I could have protected myself."

The old man's eyes go wide as his breathing gets more ragged.

"Beware Wladyslaw, the closer you get to him, the more he is likely to break the rules!" He releases your jacket and he lays back with a deep sigh.

His body begins to fade and his face smiles at you. As he disappears from view you catch the faint aroma of almonds once again.

You are in the Grand refectory, where the knights would meet and also eat their meals. It is a large, magnificent, fan-vaulted room with several columns that support the ceiling and wooden parquet flooring with vents in various places which allow hot air from the furnace vault to warm the room in winter. He turns and walks away into the garden area. You watch from the corner of the wall and see the falconer standing by the mews, looking up at the sky. He then reaches into a pouch tied to his belt and takes out something, which he then holds above his head.

He whistles in a special way a couple of times and calls the name "Tiercel". Suddenly a white bird of prey swoops down from out of the sky and perches on top of the curtain wall surrounding the garden and sits there looking down at him.

The falconer drops his hands to his sides then swings them out again to bring them back up above his head once more. You realise he is using a gesture the bird may be trained to respond to. The bird is obviously very wary and will not come down.

You look at what the falconer is holding and realise that it is a dead rat. Hunger overcomes the bird's wariness and it launches itself off the wall and comes swooping down to snatch the rat out of the falconer's hands. The bird flies up to perch on the top of the mews and gobbles the rat down. The falconer stretches his gauntleted hand out to the side of him and calls the bird by name - "Tiercel" - a couple of times.

The bird flies down and is about to land on the falconer's gauntlet, but it sees you and veers off, arrowing up into the sky and out of sight. He calls Tiercel again, but the bird does not respond. He looks around, sees you standing there and he walks over to you with a resigned expression on his ghostly face.

"I had almost got her down that time," he says, wearily. He pulls the gauntlet off his hand and drops it onto the ground at your feet. "You have a go," he tells you. "You might have a bit more luck than me!"

The falconer walks off towards the mews, fading from view as he goes.....

[MSG] cmd=SETZCOLOR a1=0 a2=16633879 a3=0 len=0
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=2424
[TEXT] 
You walk into the Komtur's office with Tiercel on your arm. At first he does not notice her but she makes a small "Chup!" sound and his head jerks up and his mouth drops open in astonishment.

"You have found her!" the Komtur says, joyously. He gets to his feet and holds his arm out to her. You wonder how the bird is going to sit on the ethereal limb when, to your utter amazement, the falcon's form starts to fade and her weight on your arm disappears, as does the leather gauntlet, which magically appears on the Komtur's outstretched arm. Tiercel's now ghostly form hops onto the Komtur's gauntleted hand and he strokes her breast in welcome, crooning to her in low tones.

The Komtur looks at you with gratitude in his eyes. "My thanks, Duke Alaric," he says, and points to the door in the North wall. "You may now continue your mission, through that door is a travel portal, which you can use to travel to other places. I wish you the best of luck, but beware that you might find peril if you use the portal."

With that he walks towards the door to the hallway. "Come, my beauty," he says to Tiercel. "Let us fly!" As he walks out of the door, his form and that of the falcon on his arm fade from view.

You hear a hush descend on the chapel as the priest enters. You expect him to start the service by speaking the Latin words of the sign of the cross, but instead he speaks to the knights.

"A carrier pigeon has just arrived from Konigsberg with an urgent message about our brothers in Toompea," he tells them. "The castle is under siege by the Sambians and we will be riding to their aid as soon as we can. Our brothers at Konigsberg are also on their way. After this service you should report to your units. Beware that the Sambians are rumoured to have captured a travel portal amulet - treat any strangers seen emerging from a travel portal as hostile, they are to be apprehended for interrogation if possible."

There is a brief buzz of conversation as the knights discuss the news, then silence again as the priest starts the mass. You sigh as you realise that they may be there for some time.

You also realise that you now cannot ask these knights for help with your quest! If you emerge from this portal they are going to think you are a Sambian infiltrator and you will be arrested. The same might happen if you go anywhere else using the amulet - maybe you should go somewhere else for now, you can come back here when the service is over?

You see a couple of men come out of a small door in the building a bit further east. They pull the cannon towards the centre of the courtyard, scattering knights and horses, all of whom protest vehemently. The rider stops the horses and turns to look at the opening, as if expecting something else to come out.

A few minutes go by and then the cook snorts and, belching loudly, gets to his feet. He takes a sip of the broth with his ladle and nods. Taking a pile of bowls from a nearby shelf, he starts to dish out portions of broth.

"OK, you miserable bunch of cut-throats," he calls out, "grub's up!".

The mercenaries get to their feet as one man with various ribald and extremely rude comments. They each take a dish of broth and sit back down to eat it. The cook joins them, obviously eager to taste his own cooking.

They all seem to be enjoying the broth, but then one of the mercenaries starts to cough and he lurches to his feet holding his throat. The other mercenaries look at him incredulously as he stands there struggling to breathe.

Then - one-by-one - they all follow suit, ending with the cook who is the last to succumb to the poison. Soon, there is silence, punctuated only by the bubbling of the broth above the firepit. The mercenaries all appear to be dead. Now it is safe to venture forth.

[MSG] cmd=SETZCOLOR a1=0 a2=16633879 a3=0 len=0
[MSG] cmd=PRINT a1=0 a2=0 a3=0 len=4668
[TEXT] 
You hear a voice from from the other end of the church and look in that direction to see that there is someone sitting in the Bishop's throne - it is the sorcerer-prince himself, Wladyslaw.

He utters a curse in a language you do not know then leaps up from the chair and stands there with a furious look on his face. You realise with surprise that Wladyslaw is only a small man - you expected someone about three metres tall and covered in hair. He wears a long black cloak and his long hair falls either side of his scarred face in tight curls.

"How the hell did you get past my guards!?" he shouts in a heavily-accented voice. "I trust they have paid with their lives for their incompetence? I suppose you think that you are going to finish me off just as easily?

He draws himself up to his full height then, muttering the words of an incantation, launches a spell at you which hurtles towards you in a shower of incandescent sparks!

You instinctively raise your shield to protect yourself and it deflects the spell away.

The sorcerer then launches a series of increasingly powerful disabling spells at you that threaten to knock the shield from your arm. You suddenly realise that the bolts of arcane energy are bouncing off the mirror you fixed to the front of your shield!

You hold your shield in front of you with both hands and advance towards the sorcerer, whose mouth gapes open and his eyes go wide with surprise.

"See how you deal with this, then," he snarls and he mutters the incantation for the most powerful death spell he knows. Flinging his arms at you he casts the spell, which roars through the air towards you.

You are only a couple of metres from him as the spell hits your shield. It hits the mirror square-on and rebounds off the mirror in a shower of deep red sparks. You hear a scream of "NO....!" which is cut off abruptly as the spell hits Wladyslaw straight in the face, killing him instantly.

He collapses to the floor of the church and you lower your shield to gaze upon his body. As you watch with horror, his skin starts to wrinkle and his body shrinks in upon itself as the spell which prolonged his life fades away. The skin eventually sloughs away from the sorcerer's bones, which themselves then start to crumble away. Soon, all that is left of Wladyslaw is his cloak and a pile of dust.
